# **Agito – Enterprise UX Operating System  
Tarih: 05.12.2025  
Hazırlayan: Murat Çetin**

---

# **Executive Summary**

Agito’nun geliştirdiği çözümler; çok modüllü iş süreçlerini, yoğun veri girişlerini ve uzman kullanıcı gruplarını destekleyen **enterprise-grade ERP bileşenleri** içerir. Mevcut durumda tasarım üretimi standartize edilmemiş, global benchmark referansları sınırlı ve modüller arasında davranışsal tutarlılık net değildir.

Bu nedenle amaç, Agito için **kurumsal ERP ihtiyaçlarına uygun**, modern B2B prensipleri ile uyumlu, geliştirme maliyetlerini düşüren ve kullanıcı verimliliğini artıran, uçtan uca bir **Enterprise UX Operating System** oluşturmaktır.

Bu sistem üç ana yapı taşına dayanır:  
1. **Framework & Guiding Principles**  
2. **Production-Friendly Design Pipeline**  
3. **Governance & Quality Gate**

İlk 90 günün odağı; temel prensiplerin, pipeline mimarisinin, pattern library’nin ve review mekanizmalarının kurulmasıdır.

---

# **Güncel Durum**

## **1. Tasarım Üretimi / Verimlilik Problemleri**
- Ant Design arayüz bileşenleri kullanılmasına rağmen, dosya düzeni ve component lifecycle sistematik değil.  
- Frame, autolayout ve component reuse aktif kullanılmıyor.  
- Ekranlar çoğunlukla manuel üretildiği için “single source of truth” yapılamıyor.  
- Bu durum hem **geliştirme maliyetini artırıyor** hem de **revizyon döngülerini manuel ve yavaş** hale getiriyor.

## **2. Benchmark Eksikliği**
- Global enterprise ürünlerle kıyas yapılmıyor.  
- ERP’ye özgü uzman kullanıcı davranışları, veri yoğunluğu, sözleşme/işlem akışları gibi kritik alanlarda **standart tasarım referansları** eksik.  
- Bu eksiklik, kaliteyi stabilize eden prensiplerin oluşmasını engelliyor.

---

# **İhtiyaç**

Agito’nun modülleri için gerekli olan:  
- **Tek bir kurumsal UX çerçevesi (Framework)**  
- **Modüler ve tekrar kullanılabilir bir tasarım pipeline’ı**  
- **Design → Development geçişini standardize eden kontrol mekanizması**  
- **Expert user davranışlarına uygun hız ve verimlilik stratejisi**  

Bu ihtiyaçlar doğrultusunda önerilen çözüm:  
→ **Agito Enterprise UX Operating System (Agito UX-OS)**.

---

# **İlk 90 Gün Çıktıları**

- Kurumsal ERP’ye özel **Agito Tasarım Framework v1**  
- Figma production architecture, naming ve documentation sistemi  
- Design Pattern Library v1 (Arama, filtre, tablo, işlem, detay)  
- Interaction & Flow Layer taslakları  
- Design Review Checklist v1  
- Benchmark kütüphanesi (10–12 referans ürün)  
- Proje başlangıç checklist seti  
- İlk governance mekanizmalarının devreye alınması

# **Framework & Guiding Principles**

## **Kurumsal ERP – Modern Tasarım Prensipleri**
ERP doğasına uygun temel tasarım kuralları:  
- **Yoğun veri giriş optimizasyonu** (field hierarchy, grouping, error prevention)  
- **Uzman kullanıcı için hız prensipleri** (keyboard-first, minimum-click workflows)  
- **Tekrarlanabilir layout sistematiği**  
- **Transaction-heavy iş akışları için risk azaltıcı desenler**  
- **State, role ve permission yapılarının UI/UX karşılığı**  
- **“Information-first, UI-second” yaklaşımı** (ERP standardı)  

Bu prensipler tüm modüller için ortak dil oluşturur.

## **Benchmark Çalışmaları**
Benchmark iki amaca hizmet eder:  
1. **Global ERP + insurance enterprise standardı yakalamak**  
2. Agito özelinde **en iyi pratikleri pattern hâline dönüştürmek**

Benchmark kapsamları:  
- SAP, Oracle, Workday, Odoo, Salesforce  
- Allianz global dijital ürünleri  
- Enterprise veri giriş, tablo ve işlem ekranları  

## **Expert User Persona Odağı**
- Günlük işlem hacmi çok yüksek.  
- Hız, kestirimsel davranış, alışkanlık tabanlı kullanım kritik.  
- Klavye-first & mouse-shortcut kombinasyonları gerekli.  
- Yoğun ekranlarda “görsel gürültü azaltma” ve “taranabilirlik” öncelikli.  

Framework bu personayı merkeze alır.

---

# **Production-Friendly Design Pipeline**

Pipeline’ın amacı:  
→ **Modüler, scalable ve üretim dostu tek bir tasarım üretim sistemi kurmak.**

---

## **Benchmarking (Pipeline içine entegre)**  
Her yeni modül/feature:  
1. Benchmark →  
2. Prensip çıkarımı →  
3. Pattern Library’ye eklenme →  
4. Üretime girme  
şeklinde standardize edilmiş bir döngü ile ilerler.

---

## **Design Production Architecture**
- **Figma Mimari Hiyerarşisi**  
  - Workspace → Project → Production Pages → Exports  
- **Component Lifecycle Yönetimi**  
  - Doğum / Kullanım / Versiyonlama / Emeklilik  
- **Naming Standartları**  
  - Ant Design + Agito Prefix  
- **Documentation Layer**  
  - Her component için usage, limits, best practices açıklamaları  

Amaç:  
→ Tasarım dosyalarını **single source of truth** haline getirmek.

---

## **Interaction & Flow Layer**
(reusable, scalable, efficiency-driven)

- **Veri Giriş Prensipleri**  
- **Form Yoğunluk Yönetimi** (single-page vs multi-step)  
- **Error Handling Sistematiği** (inline, banner, transaction-level)  
- **Transaction & İşlem Akışları için Interaction Blocks**  
- **Role-based UI davranışı**  

---

## **Pattern Library**
Tüm ERP modüllerine uygulanabilir reusable pattern seti:

- **Arama** (global + domain search)  
- **Filtre** (quick filters, advanced filters)  
- **Tablo** (data density, column behavior, bulk actions)  
- **Detay Görünümleri** (summary-first, side-by-side layout)  
- **İşlem Ekranları** (transaction chains, step-flow patterns)  

Pattern Library hem tasarım hızını hem tutarlılığı artırır.

---

# **Governance & Quality Gate**

Amaç:  
→ Üretim maliyetini düşürmek, hata oranını azaltmak, tutarlılığı güçlendirmek.

---

## **Proje Başlangıç Checklist**
- Feature scope  
- Role & permission analizi  
- Benchmark kontrolü  
- Pattern seçimi  
- Interaction flow doğrulaması  

---

## **Design Review Checklist**
- Component usage doğruluğu  
- Autolayout ve naming kontrolü  
- Interaction flow hataları  
- Pattern uyumluluğu  
- Edge case + error handling  
- Developer handoff temizliği  

---

## **60–90 Days (Scaling)**

# ✅ **3. Production-Friendly Design Pipeline – *Nasıl Çizeceksin?***

Bu bölüm **FigJam’de bir “yatay boru hattı” (pipeline)** gibi gözükmeli.

### 📐 Adım adım çizim:

1. **Kanvasın ortasında geniş bir yatay rectangle çiz.**  
   Genişliği büyük olsun (1200px gibi).

2. Bu rectangle’ı **dört eşit şeride ayır** (swimlane).  
   Sol tarafa lane başlıklarını yaz:  
   - Benchmark  
   - Design Architecture  
   - Interaction & Flow Layer  
   - Pattern Library

3. Her lane’in içine **kutucuklar** yerleştir → her kutucuk bir aşamayı temsil eder.

Örnek görsel (ASCII):

```
 ---------------------------------------------------------
| Benchmark                                                |
|  [Global UX Best Practices] → [ERP Competitor Review]    |
 ---------------------------------------------------------
| Design Architecture                                       |
|  [Figma Structure] → [Component Lifecycle] → [Naming]     |
 ---------------------------------------------------------
| Interaction & Flow Layer                                  |
|  [Form Model] → [Data Inputs] → [Error Handling System]   |
 ---------------------------------------------------------
| Pattern Library                                           |
|  [Search] [Filter] [Table] [Detail] [Action Patterns]     |
 ---------------------------------------------------------
```

🎨 **Görsel ipucu:**  
Kutuları *mor* yap → aralarına ok ekle → çok profesyonel görünür.

# ✅ **4. Interaction & Flow Layer – *Bu tam olarak nasıl görünür?***

Bu bölümü **3 büyük baloncuk + bağlantılar** şeklinde yapacaksın.

### 📐 Adım adım:

1. Büyük 3 adet oval shape çiz:
   - Veri Girişleri
   - Yoğun Form Akışları
   - Error-Handling

2. Bu üç balonun arasını oklarla bağla:

```
[ Veri Girişleri ] → [ Form Akışı ] → [ Error Handling ]
```

3. Her balonun içine küçük sticky notlar koy:
   - Veri Girişleri → dropdown, autocomplete, masked input
   - Form Akışı → stepper, inline validation
   - Error Handling → field-level vs global

🎨 **Görsel ipucu:**  
Balonların çevresine hafif shadow ver (FigJam’de shape shadow).  
“Domain architecture map” gibi görünür.

# ✅ **1. Design Production Architecture – (İkon: “Blueprint + Layers”)**

**En doğru metafor:**  
📐 **Blueprint / Structure Plan** + 📚 **Katman İkonu**

### Kullanılabilir ikon tipleri:
- 📐 **Blueprint** (mimari plan çizgileri)  
- 🧱 **Layered Blocks** (katmanlar)  
- 🗂️ **Component Grid** (9-dots grid / layout grid)
- 🧩 **Component puzzle**

### Neden bu ikon?  
Çünkü bu başlık; dosya mimarisi, component lifecycle, naming system ve “architectural design thinking” anlatıyor.

**FigJam önerisi:**  
“Blueprint” + küçük “layers” ikonunu üst üste koy → profesyonel görünür.

---

# ✅ **2. Proje Başlangıç Checklist – (İkon: “Checklist + Flag”)**

En iyi metafor:  
📝 **Checklist** + 🚩 **Project Start Flag**

### Kullanılabilir ikon tipleri:
- ☑️ Tick list / to-do list  
- 🏁 Start flag  
- 📄 Document with checkmarks  
- 🎯 Target + check

### Neden bu ikon?  
Bu başlık; proje başlangıç koşulları, gereksinimler, netlik ve kickoff aşamalarını temsil eder.

FigJam’de en iyi:  
📝 Checklist belgesi.

---

# ✅ **3. Interaction & Flow Layer – (İkon: “Arrows + Nodes”)**

Metafor:  
➡️ **Akış okları** + 🔘 **Bağlantı noktaları**

### Kullanılabilir ikon tipleri:
- 🔀 Flow-diagram icon  
- 🕸️ Nodes connected  
- ↗️↘️ Çoklu oklarla bağlanan grafik  
- 🔄 Interaction arrows

### Neden bu ikon?  
Interaction → davranış, Flow → akış bağlantıları.  
UX mimarisine en çok uyan evrensel sembol: **flow-chart icon**.

FigJam için öneri:  
“Flowchart nodes” icon (3 node + arrows).

---

# ✅ **4. Design Review Checklist – (İkon: “Magnifying Glass + Check”)**

Metafor:  
🔍 **Review** + ☑️ **Design Validation**

### Kullanılabilir ikon tipleri:
- 🔍 Magnifier  
- 🔍 + ☑️ combined (Figma’da var)  
- 👁️ Eye + check  
- 📋 Checklist + magnifier overlay

### Neden bu ikon?  
Design Review = kalite kontrol + inceleme + doğrulama.

FigJam’de en doğru görüntü:  
🔍&☑️ aynı ikon (Noun Project’te “review approved”).

---

# ✅ **5. Pattern Library – (İkon: “Blocks / UI Components / Lego”)**

Metafor:  
🧩 **Reusable Components** + 🧱 **Blocks**

### Kullanılabilir ikon tipleri:
- 🧱 Component blocks  
- 🧩 Puzzle piece  
- 📦 UI component box  
- 3-grid layout icon (UI pattern için)

### Neden bu ikon?  
Pattern library demek: reusable, modular, repeatable building blocks.

FigJam için en iyi ikon:  
🧩 Puzzle piece veya UI component grid.

# **“Single Source of Truth” (SSOT) Nedir?**

**Tanım (Basit ve Yönetici-Dostu):**  
Bir bilgi veya ekranın **tek bir doğru kaynağı** olmasıdır.  
Yani bir ekran, component, akış veya veri nerede tanımlanıyorsa herkes **o tek kaynağa bakarak** çalışır.

**Amaç:**  
👉 Aynı ekranın *3 farklı versiyonu* olmasın.  
👉 Geliştirici, analist, QA ve tasarımcı **aynı dosyaya** güvenebilsin.  
👉 Revizyon tek yerden yapılsın, diğer her yerde otomatik güncellensin.  

---

# **Neden Önemlidir?**

### **1. Revizyon maliyetini dramatik şekilde düşürür.**  
Bir ekran 4 yerde değil, **tek yerde değiştirilir**. Hata riski minimuma iner.

### **2. Tasarım – Geliştirme – QA arasındaki uyuşmazlığı yok eder.**  
Herkesin baktığı kaynak tek olduğu için “Hangisi güncel?” sorusu biter.

### **3. Tutarlılığı otomatik hale getirir.**  
Tüm modüller aynı pattern ve component setlerini kullanır → sistem bütünlüğü oluşur.

### **4. Üretim hızını artırır.**  
Ekip yeni bir ekran tasarlarken sıfırdan çizmek yerine **mevcut kaynakları reuse eder**.

---

# **Agito Özelinde SSOT’nin Karşılığı**

✔ Figma’da **tek bir Production File** + Pattern Library  
✔ Tüm modüllerin ortak kullandığı **component lifecycle**  
✔ Analist, geliştirici, QA için **tek güncel referans**  

Bugün:  
- Aynı bileşenin “çoklu versiyonları” var → hata riski yüksek.  
- Ekranların güncel hâli her ekipte farklı olabilir.

Yeni sistemde:  
→ **Tasarım değişikliği = Tek dosya → tüm modüller güncellenir.**

---

# **Sunumda Nasıl Kısaca Yazılır?**  
**“Single Source of Truth, tasarım ve geliştirme ekiplerinin aynı doğrulanmış kaynaktan çalışmasını sağlayan sistemdir.  
Tüm ekranlar, componentler ve akışlar tek bir Figma üretim dosyasında tutulur.  
Böylece revizyon maliyeti azalır, tutarlılık artar ve ekipler arasında bilgi farkı ortadan kalkar.”**

# ✔ **Frame / Autolayout / Component Reuse → Agito’ya Göre Ne Demek?**

## **1) Frame (Ekran Çerçevesi) – “Ekranın iskeleti”**
**Ne işe yarar?**  
Bir ekranın düzenini, sınırlarını ve yapısal boyutunu belirleyen ana konteynırdır.

**Neden kritik?**  
Frame kullanılmazsa ekranlar:
- Dağınık olur  
- Taşınması zor olur  
- Geliştirici ile ekran birebir eşleşmez

**Kısa tanım:**  
➡ *“Ekranın teknik ve görsel iskeletidir.”*

---

## **2) Auto-Layout – “Mühendis mantığıyla kendini düzenleyen ekran”**
**Ne işe yarar?**  
Elemanların birbiriyle doğru hizada kalmasını, taşındığında veya metin uzadığında otomatik olarak düzenlenmesini sağlar.

**Neden kritik?**  
Manuel çizimde:
- Her minik değişiklikte tüm dizilim bozulur  
- Revizyon maliyeti katlanarak artar  

Auto-layout’ta:
- Ekran kendi kendini toplar  
- Geliştirmedeki grid/spacing birebir uyumlu olur  

**Kısa tanım:**  
➡ *“Ekranın kendi kendini kontrol eden düzen sistemi.”*

---

## **3) Component Reuse – “Bir kez yap, her yerde kullan”**
**Ne işe yarar?**  
Buton, tablo header’ı, form alanı gibi her bir UI parçasının **tek merkezden yönetilmesi**.

**Neden kritik?**  
Tekrarlayan çizim → zaman kaybı + tutarsızlık  
Reusability → hız + görünüm standardı + tek noktadan güncelleme

**Kısa tanım:**  
➡ *“Aynı UI elemanını tekrar tekrar çizmek yerine, tek kaynaktan kullanmak.”*

---

# ✔ Figjam veya rapor için ultra kısa versiyon:

### **Frame:**  
Ekranın teknik iskeletidir. Tüm modüllerde tutarlı bir yapı sağlar.

### **Auto-Layout:**  
Ekranın kendi kendini düzenlemesini sağlayan sistemdir; revizyon maliyetini düşürür.

### **Component Reuse:**  
UI parçalarının tek merkezden yönetilmesi; hız, tutarlılık ve düşük geliştirme maliyeti sağlar.

## ✅ *Frame nedir?* (Basit anlatım)
**Frame**, Figma’da “bir kutu”, “bir konteyner”, “bir modül alanı”dır.

- Ekran = bir frame olabilir  
- Sidebar = bir frame olabilir  
- Tablo başlığı = bir frame olabilir  
- Kart yapısı = bir frame olabilir  

**Kısacası:**  
> *Frame, ekrandaki her şeyi düzenli ve kurallı bir şekilde tutan en temel yapı taşıdır.*

**Neden önemli?**  
Frame kullanılmazsa geliştirme tarafında ekranın yapısı bozulur, spacing tutmaz ve tasarım kodla birebir aktarılamaz.

---

## ✅ *Auto-layout nedir?* (Basit anlatım)
Auto-layout, Figma’da **tasarımın kendini otomatik hizalaması, genişleyip daralması**dır.

- İçeriğe göre buton boyu otomatik artar
- Satırlar eşit hizalanır
- Responsive davranış simüle edilir

**Neden önemli?**  
> Kod tarafında zaten her şey auto-layout mantığıyla yapılır (flexbox).  
> Tasarım tarafı auto-layout kullanmazsa geliştirici tasarımı birebir aktaramaz → zaman kaybı.

---

## ✅ *Component reuse nedir?* (Basit anlatım)
Bir kez yapılan tasarım parçasının (buton, modal, kart, form alanı) tekrar tekrar kullanılabilmesidir.

**Neden kritik?**

- Aynı buton 10 kez sıfırdan yapılmaz → *hız*
- Tüm projede aynı görünüm korunur → *tutarlılık*
- Geliştirme için tek referans olur → *tek doğruluk noktası (SSOT)*  
- Bir değişiklik yapıldığında *her yere otomatik yansır*

---

> Bu üçü olmazsa tasarım dağılır, ekranlar birbirini tutmaz ve geliştirme maliyeti artar.

**Not:** Group, component değildir; tekrar kullanılabilirlik sağlamaz ama düzen sağlar.

# **1. Framework & Guiding Principles**  
*Kurumsal ERP ürünleri için mimari tasarım standardı*

---

## **1.1 Agito Tasarım Framework v1 (Kurumsal ERP’ye Özel)**
ERP bağlamına özel temel yapı taşları:

- **Modülerlik İlkesi:**  
  Her ekran, form ve işlem akışı modüler tasarlanır; yeniden kullanılabilir parçalara ayrılır.

- **High-Density UI Tasarımı:**  
  Uzman kullanıcı profili nedeniyle “bilgi yoğun” ekranların düzeni, hiyerarşisi ve boşluk oranları optimize edilir.

- **Task-based Arayüz Yapısı:**  
  Kullanıcı ekranları “iş tamamlamaya” odaklı ilerler; bilgi gösteriminden çok iş akışı tasarımı öncelenir.

- **Transactional Flow Odaklılık:**  
  Poliçe, sözleşme, teklif, talep gibi işlem tiplerinin kendine özgü davranış modelleri tanımlanır.

- **Tipik ERP Kullanıcı Davranışları İçin Optimizasyon:**  
  Uzun gövdeli tablolarda hızlı tarama, kısayol destekleri, bulk action, filtre–arama döngüleri.

---

## **1.2 Guiding Principles (Tasarım Üretiminde Standardizasyon)**
Tasarım ekibinin her projede aynı kaliteyi üretmesini sağlayan prensipler:

- **Consistency First:**  
  Aynı veri tipi → aynı komponent.  
  Aynı işlem → aynı pattern.

- **Single Final Source of Truth:**  
  Sprint sonunda finalize edilen tasarım → dokümantasyon görevi görür → tüm ekip için referans olur.

- **Production Reality Alignment:**  
  Tasarım, geliştirilebilirlik kurallarına göre üretilir (auto-layout, constraints, responsive, reusable yapı).

- **Clarity Over Decoration:**  
  ERP’de amaç: hız, doğruluk ve iş tamamlama → gereksiz görsel karmaşa yok.

- **Scalability Mindset:**  
  Tasarımın gelecekteki modüllere taşınabilir olması önceliklendirilir.

---

## **1.3 Benchmark Kütüphanesi (Global ERP Karşılaştırmaları)**
Her yeni tasarım kararını doğrulamak için oluşturulan referans havuzu:

- SAP Fiori Patterns  
- Oracle ERP Cloud UI  
- Workday  
- Microsoft Dynamics  
- Odoo Enterprise  
- Ant Design Enterprise Patterns  

Benchmark kullanım amaçları:

- Veri yoğun arayüzlerde doğru düzeni doğrulamak  
- Expert user davranışlarını modellemek  
- Pattern library’nin eksik noktalarını belirlemek  
- Global ERP yaklaşımıyla hizalanmak

---

## **1.4 Expert User Çalışma Prensipleri**
ERP kullanıcılarının davranışlarına özel tasarım ilkeleri:

- **Hız önceliklidir:** Mouse + klavye hibrit kullanım desteklenmeli.
- **Yoğun veri işlenir:** Tablolar, form alanları, bulk işlemler optimize edilmeli.
- **Minimum tıklama:** “Single action / minimal path” stratejisi.
- **Hata yapma maliyeti yüksek:** Error-handling ve doğrulama erken yapılmalı.
- **Tekrar eden işler çoktur:** Kısayollar, varsayılan dolu alanlar, template yaklaşımı.

---

---

# **2. Production-Friendly Design Pipeline**  
*Tasarım üretimini hızlandıran ve scalable hale getiren sistem*

---

## **2.1 Figma Production Architecture v1**
**(dosya yapılanması, component lifecycle, naming, documentation)**

- **Dosya Yapılanması Standardı:**  
  Product → Modules → Screens → Components → Assets hiyerarşisi.

- **Component Lifecycle Sistemi:**  
  Draft → Proposed → Approved → Versioned → Deprecated döngüsü.

- **Naming Conventions:**  
  UI component, variant, state ve layer isimlendirme standartları.

- **Documentation Layer:**  
  Her bileşende: kullanım amacı, props, davranış kuralları, edge-case tanımları.

- **Frame / Auto-layout / Group Kuralları:**  
  Kod-aligned, responsive ve scalable ekran üretimi için zorunlu kurallar.

---

## **2.2 Design Pattern Library v1**  
(Arama, filtre, tablo, detay, işlem)

Tüm ürünlerde tekrar kullanılan UI/UX pattern setleri:

- **Arama Patterni:**  
  Basit arama, gelişmiş arama, parametre bazlı arama, öneri listesi.

- **Filtre Patterni:**  
  Inline filtre, slide-over filtre, saved filters, kombinasyonlu filtreler.

- **Tablo Patterni:**  
  Kolon yönetimi, bulk action, satır detayları, tablo içi edit, pagination.

- **Detay Sayfaları:**  
  Summary block, history, ilişkili kayıtlar, status management.

- **İşlem Akışları:**  
  Tek adımlı işlem, çok adımlı wizard, doğrulama adımları, context-based action menüleri.

---

## **2.3 Interaction & Flow Layer (taslaklar)**  
*(yoğun form akışları, veri girişleri, error handling)*

- **Yoğun Form Akışları:**  
  Çok alanlı, dinamik ve dependency içeren form tasarımları için standart hiyerarşi.

- **Veri Girişleri:**  
  Masked input, dropdown, free text, autocomplete, relation-Link input kural setleri.

- **Error Handling:**  
  Inline validation, form-level validation, transaction errors, API error feedback.

- **Transactional Flow Logic:**  
  ERP işlem döngüleri için tasarlanmış flow modelleme (create–review–approve–close).

---

---

# **3. Governance & Quality Gate**  
*Tasarım çıktılarını güvence altına alan kontrol mekanizmaları*

---

## **3.1 Design Review Checklist v1**
Kalite standardını koruyan kontrol seti:

- Figma yapısal kurallarına uyum  
- Pattern library uyumu  
- Naming & documentation kontrolü  
- Interaction doğrulama  
- Veri modeline uyum  
- Edge-case değerlendirmesi  
- Developer handoff kontrolü

---

## **3.2 Proje Başlangıç Checklist v1**
Yeni modül veya ürün başlamadan önce yapılan zorunlu kontroller:

- Gereksinimlerin pattern library ile eşleşmesi  
- Benchmark doğrulaması  
- Veri modeli uyum analizi  
- Transactional flow mapping  
- Modüller arası bağımlılık analizi  
- İlk risk değerlendirmesi  

---

## **3.3 Governance Mekanizmaları (Handoff & Revizyon Maliyetini Düşürme)**
İlk devreye alınacak süreçler:

- **Design Gate:**  
  Tasarım onaylanmadan geliştirme başlamaz.

- **Freeze Point:**  
  Sprint sonunda finalize edilen tasarım → tüm ekip için tek referans.

- **Versioning Kuralı:**  
  Her component değişikliği versiyonlanır, dev-ekip kırılmaz.

- **Standard Template Kullanımı:**  
  Ekranlar aynı isim, aynı layout, aynı pattern setiyle üretilir.

# **Agito Enterprise Design Framework (A-EDF)**  
**ERP-level Design Standards & Production Pipeline**

---

# **📌 Executive Summary**

Agito’nun geliştirdiği çözümler; çok modüllü iş akışlarını, yoğun veri girişlerini ve uzman kullanıcı rollerini barındıran **enterprise-grade ERP uygulamalarıdır**. Mevcut durumda tasarım üretimi standartize edilmemiş, global benchmark referansları sınırlı kalmış ve tasarımın üretimle ilişkisinde net bir sistem bulunmamaktadır.

Bu nedenle ilk 90 gün içinde hedefimiz:  
- **Kurumsal ERP’ye özel tasarım framework’ünü** oluşturmak,  
- Tasarım üretimini **modüler, tekrar kullanılabilir ve production-friendly** hale getirmek,  
- Ekipler arası kalite ve uyumu artıracak **governance mekanizmalarını** devreye almaktır.

---

# **📍 Güncel Durum (Problem Alanları)**

### **1. Tasarım Üretimi Standart Değil**
- Ant Design kullanılmasına rağmen **dosya düzeni, component lifecycle, naming ve documentation** sistematik değil.  
- Frame / Auto-layout / Group yapıları tutarsız kullanılıyor.  
- Ekranlar manuel üretildiği için **tek bir referans kaynağı (single source of truth)** oluşmuyor.  
- Bu durum hem geliştirme maliyetini artırıyor hem de revizyon döngülerini manuel ve yavaş hale getiriyor.

### “Single Source of Truth” Açıklaması  
Finalize olmuş her sprintte:  
**tasarım dosyası → geliştirmenin temel aldığı tek resmi kaynak olmalıdır.**  
Herhangi bir ekranın farklı versiyonları farklı yerlerde bulunmamalıdır.

### **2. Benchmark ile Validasyon Eksik**
- Global ERP ürünleriyle kıyaslama yapılmadığı için kaliteyi sabitleyen prensipler oluşmamış durumda.  
- Yoğun veri giriş akışları, sözleşme/işlem süreçleri, riskli adımlarda hata önleme gibi konularda **uluslararası referans eksikliği** mevcut.

# **1. Framework & Guiding Principles**

## **1.1 Agito Tasarım Framework v1**
ERP bağlamına özel; tutarlılık, veri yoğunluğu, hız ve doğruluk odaklı bir tasarım çekirdeği oluşturulur.

Bu framework:  
- Tüm modüller arasında ortak davranış modelini tanımlar.  
- Yeni ekran tasarımında ekip için **başlangıç noktası** olur.  
- Tasarım ve geliştirme arasında aynı dili oluşturur.

---

## **1.2 Guiding Principles Seti**
Tasarım üretiminde herkesin aynı kalite seviyesinde hareket etmesini sağlayan kurallar setidir.

Örnek ilkeler:  
- **Clarity First:** Ekran kalabalığını azaltma, gereksiz görselleri kaldırma.  
- **Speed by Default:** Expert user için klavye kısayolları, hızlı erişim.  
- **Consistency Over Creativity:** Modüller arasındaki davranışların standart olması.  
- **Error-Free Flow:** Riskli işlem akışlarında hata önleyici tasarım.

Bu prensipler, hem tasarımcı hem de ekip için kalite çıpası görevindedir.

---

## **1.3 Benchmark Kütüphanesinin Oluşturulması**
10–12 küresel ERP / B2B platformu incelenerek:

- Veri yoğunluğu yönetimi  
- Form tasarımı  
- Tablo ve liste davranışları  
- Error-handling  
- Navigation & module hierarchy  
- Task-based ekran tasarımı  

konularında referans seti hazırlanır.

Bu set:  
**Her yeni modül için validasyon rehberi olur.**

---

## **1.4 Expert User Tasarım Prensipleri**

ERP’de kullanımın büyük çoğunluğu **uzman kullanıcılar** tarafından yapılır. Bu nedenle:

### **⚡ Hız Odaklı Tasarım**
- Gereksiz tıklama azaltılır.  
- Klavye + mouse hibrit kullanım desteklenir.  
- Kritik alanlarda görsel gürültü azaltılır.

### **📊 Yoğun Verinin Yönetimi**
- Tablolarda inline edit  
- Bulk action (toplu işlem)  
- Sık kullanılan filtrelerin kaydedilebilir olması

### **🛑 Hata Önleyici Yaklaşım**
- Riskli işlemler için doğrulama  
- Tutarlı uyarı mekanizmaları  
- Error-first tasarım prensipleri

### **🔬 Research Destekli Yaklaşım**
- Expert-user davranışlarına yönelik mikro müşteri araştırmaları  
- SAP, Oracle, Workday gibi global sistemlerin incelenmesi  
- Agito modüllerindeki en sık kullanılan akışların analiz edilmesi

Bu çıktıların tamamı **Agito Tasarım Framework v1** içine entegre edilir.

---

# **2. Production-Friendly Design Pipeline**

Amaç:  
Tasarım üretimini **modüler, ölçeklenebilir, tekrar kullanılabilir ve geliştirici dostu** hale getirmek.

---

## **2.1 Design Production Architecture v1**
Aşağıdaki yapılar net olarak tanımlanır:

### **📁 Dosya Yapılanması**
- Project → Pages → Sections → Frames  
- Her ekranın tek bir resmi kaynağı (single source) olması  
- Component ve pattern klasörlerinin ayrılması

### **📦 Component Lifecycle**
- Raw → Component → Variant → Pattern → Production  
- Componentlerin nasıl oluşturulacağı ve güncelleneceği belirlenir.

### **🏷️ Naming Standard**
- Ekranlar, componentler, katmanlar, ikonlar için ortak adlandırma sistemi.  
- Developer’ın aynı ismi Figma’da, kodda ve dokümanda görmesi sağlanır.

### **📘 Documentation**
- Her component için kısa kullanım notları  
- Patternler için davranış kuralları  
- Benchmark referansları

Bu mimari Figma’yı **bir üretim sistemi** haline getirir.

---

## **2.2 Interaction & Flow Layer Taslakları**
ERP’de en kritik tasarım katmanıdır. Aşağıda üç ana alanda standartlar oluşturulur:

### **🔹 Yoğun Form Akışları**
- Form hiyerarşisi  
- Zorunlu alan davranışları  
- Long-form bölme kuralları  
- Validation düzeni

### **🔹 Veri Girişleri**
- Inline düzenlemeler  
- Klavye kısayolları  
- Alan sıralaması (tab order)  
- Repetitive task optimization

### **🔹 Error Handling**
- Error türlerinin sınıflandırması  
- Uyarı → Riskli İşlem → Bloklama hiyerarşisi  
- Tutarlı mesaj formatı  
- Hata öncesi önleme mekanizmaları

---

## **2.3 Design Pattern Library v1**
Aşağıdaki reusable pattern setleri oluşturulur:

### **🔎 Arama Patternleri**
- Basic search  
- Advanced search  
- Saved search

### **⚙️ Filtre Patternleri**
- Inline filter  
- Persistent filter  
- Multi-select filter

### **📊 Tablo Patternleri**
- Sort  
- Group  
- Bulk action  
- Inline edit  
- Jumplink

### **📄 Detay Ekranları**
- Panel yapı  
- Object summary  
- Critical info-first düzeni

### **🔁 İşlem Patternleri**
- Onay akışları  
- Riskli işlem uyarıları  
- Task-based transaction ekranları

Pattern Library v1 → tasarım hızını artırır, geliştiriciye netlik sağlar ve tutarlılığı garanti eder.

# ✅ **How to Set UI Standards From Scratch  
(When the Source Is Figma Make / Auto-Generated UI)**

### **Problem**
- Figma Make or auto-generated UIs export frames **~2000px** (or arbitrary widths).  
- These outputs **do not reflect any UX standard**, and they break consistency in:
  - Responsive behavior  
  - Grid & spacing  
  - Typography scale  
  - Component sizes  
  - Developer implementation  

You must **normalize all screens** into a **1440px master frame**, because 1440 is the global desktop design standard for ERP/UI-heavy systems.

---

# ⭐ **THE WORKFLOW (Start → Finish)**  
This is the exact sequencing senior product companies follow.

---

# **1️⃣ Establish the Master Frame Standard (1440px)**

### **Why 1440?**
- Global standard for enterprise web (SAP Fiori, Oracle, Salesforce Lightning)
- Balanced between readability + information density  
- Works well with 12-column grids

### **Your Rule Moving Forward**
**Every design MUST start inside a 1440px master frame.**  
This becomes the **Agito Single Source of Truth Layout**.

### **Define the frame:**
- **Frame width:** 1440px  
- **Grid:** 12 columns  
- **Column width:** 80–96px (depending on complexity)  
- **Gutters:** 24px  
- **Margins:** 80–120px

→ Document this in your **Design Production Architecture** as a locked template.

---

# **2️⃣ Normalize Figma Make Screens Into the Standard Framework**

### **The key principle:**  
**Raw auto-generated screens are INPUTS, not final designs.**

### The workflow you should apply:
1. Create a new 1440 Master Frame  
2. Place the Figma Make export inside it  
3. Resize content manually using:
   - Constraints  
   - Auto-layout conversion  
   - Grid alignments  
4. Evaluate:
   - spacing  
   - hierarchy  
   - component structure  
5. Replace incorrect or oversized elements with your standard components  
6. Delete raw artifacts

### Your goal:
Turn the Figma Make screen into a **properly structured, reusable**, “Figma-native” screen.

---

# **3️⃣ Create Your UI Standards Before Designing Anything**

Here are the **minimum standards** to define **inside your Design Architecture v1**:

### **Typography Scale**
- H1 / H2 / H3 / Body / Caption  
- Use rem-based scales (12/14/16/20/24/32)

➡ Document them in a `/foundations/typography` page.

---

### **Spacing System**
Use a **4 or 8px scale**.  
Define tokens:
- spacing-4  
- spacing-8  
- spacing-12  
- spacing-16  
- spacing-24  
- spacing-32  
…

➡ This lets developers and designers speak the “same spacing language.”

---

### **Component Sizing**
Define canonical sizes:
- Input (height 40/48)  
- Button (S/M/L)  
- Table header height  
- Table row height  
- Modal widths  
- Form max-widths  

➡ With screenshots + explanation.

---

### **Color & Semantic Tokens**
- Primary  
- Secondary  
- Destructive  
- Warning  
- Info  
- Success  

This is **not branding** — this is **ERP function-driven coloring**.

---

# **4️⃣ Build the Component Lifecycle Rules**
To avoid chaos later, define how components enter and leave your system.

### Define:
- **Atomic components** (button, input, checkbox)  
- **Molecules** (search bar, filter group)  
- **Organisms** (table, detail view, form cluster)  
- **Templates** (master-detail, list-view, form pages)

Document:
- Creation rules  
- Versioning  
- Naming  
- Replacement rules  
- Deprecation rules  

Example naming:
```
cmp/button/primary/default
cmp/input/text/default
cmp/table/default
```

---

# **5️⃣ Create the 1440 Wireframe Template Library**

Before touching UI detail, create:
- **List layout** templates  
- **Form layout** templates  
- **Table + Action bar** templates  
- **Master-detail template**  
- **Dashboard template**

These allow you to map Business → UX → UI quickly.

---

# **6️⃣ Production Documentation Rules**

### Every screen must come with:
- Purpose  
- Flow  
- Interaction rules  
- Error-handling  
- Validation  
- Data states (empty, loading, success, error)  
- Expected user type (expert or novice)  

This becomes a **developer-ready deliverable**.

---

# **7️⃣ Lock the System With Governance**

Tighten quality gates:
- No design delivered without 1440 frame  
- No screen with “freehand spacing”  
- No random components  
- No Figma Make leftovers  
- Everything must be aligned to:
  - grid  
  - spacing tokens  
  - component library  
  - interaction rules  

This creates “Agito UI Law.”

---

# 🚀 **Your Immediate Action Items (Next 48 Hours)**

### **1. Build the 1440px Master Frame**  
Include the grid & template page.

### **2. Create Foundations v1**
- Typography  
- Spacing  
- Colors  
- Grid  
- Frame rules

### **3. Start converting the first Figma Make screen**  
Follow trimming → resizing → standardizing → componentizing.

### **4. Begin documenting the Architecture v1 page**  
This is your first major deliverable.

### 190. **ASSISTANT / NOTE:**

Here is the **real, technical, executive-level explanation** of **why 1440px is the global standard** for enterprise web design — not an opinion, but based on **UI density, readability, engineering alignment, and historical platform convention**.

This is the version you can *confidently tell CTOs, architects, and developers*.

---

# ✅ **Why 1440px Is the Standard for Enterprise & ERP UI Design**

1440px is used because it is the **optimal balance between:**
- information density (needed for ERP)  
- readability  
- universal device compatibility  
- developer implementation  
- responsive behavior  
- industry conventions  

Let’s break it down properly.

---

# **1️⃣ Because 1440px is the *largest safe baseline* across modern laptop screens**

When designing enterprise systems, you want a base width that works on almost every workstation developers and operators use.

**Most common enterprise laptop widths:**  
- 1366px  
- 1440px  
- 1536px  
- 1680px  
- 1920px (desktop monitors)

**1440px is the largest width that is still completely readable on:**
- 1366px laptops (after responsive scale)  
- 1440px laptops  
- 1536px screens  
- 1920px workplace monitors  

This makes it the **universally compatible working canvas**.

---

# **2️⃣ Because all major enterprise UI systems use it**

Here is the key part you can tell architects:

### **1440px is the default design width in global enterprise design systems:**
- **SAP Fiori**  
- **Salesforce Lightning**  
- **Oracle Redwood UI**  
- **Microsoft Fluent (web)**  
- **Atlassian**  
- **IBM Carbon**  
- **ServiceNow**  

All of them use:
- **12-column grid**
- **1440px baseline**
- Flexible margins inside for responsiveness

Why?  
Because ERP users work with:
- tables  
- dense forms  
- transactional flows  
- multi-panel layouts  

These need a **wide but controlled canvas**.

---

# **3️⃣ Because 1440px allows the perfect 12-column grid**

This is the *real* reason designers don’t say publicly.

**1440px → 12 columns → 24px gutters → 80–96px columns**  
Everything divides cleanly.

Starts clean.  
Scales clean.  
Developers love it.  

If you use 2000px or 1600px or random widths from auto-generated screens:
- columns get uneven  
- spacing breaks  
- responsive behavior becomes painful  
- components don’t fit cleanly  
- tables and forms lose predictable alignment

1440px gives a perfect mathematical base.

---

# **4️⃣ Because enterprise users need maximum horizontal space, but not full-screen chaos**

ERP ≠ marketing website.  
ERP ≠ mobile-first app.

ERP users (finance, operations, insurance, banking, energy) need:
- wide tables  
- left navigation  
- right drawers  
- action bars  
- detail panels  

**1440px = enough space, without causing scanning fatigue.**

Designing at 1920px causes:
- long eye travel  
- broken hierarchy  
- inconsistent component usage  
- too much whitespace  
- unreadable extra-wide content  

1440 keeps the cognitive load stable.

---

# **5️⃣ Because responsive scaling is predictable**

From 1440px, you can scale down using:
- 1280px breakpoint
- 1024px breakpoint
- 768px breakpoint

**All standard breakpoints fall nicely under 1440.**

If your base screen is 2000px:
- scaling down breaks layout  
- components stretch unpredictably  
- tables need manual resizing  
- grid no longer maps  

---

# **6️⃣ Because it keeps development consistent and cheap**

Developers prefer a **fixed design baseline**.

1440px ensures:
- predictable column widths  
- predictable layout behavior  
- consistent component sizes  
- reduced CSS overrides  
- easier responsive implementation  

This reduces:
- implementation cost  
- QA cost  
- UI bugs  
- unexpected overflow issues  

---

# **7️⃣ Because it is the de-facto global convention**

You want Agito to look like it knows the global rules of enterprise product design.

Using 1440px signals:
> “This team understands enterprise design standards.”

Using 2000px signals:
> “This design is auto-generated, unstructured, and not production-ready.”

---

# TL;DR (for CTO slide)

### **Why 1440px?**  
Because 1440px is the **global enterprise standard** used by SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, IBM, Microsoft, and Atlassian since it provides:  
- optimal horizontal workspace for expert users  
- a perfect 12-column grid  
- predictable responsive scaling  
- compatibility across all enterprise laptop/desktop sizes  
- lower development cost  
- stable component behavior

# ✅ **Production-Friendly Design Pipeline — Week 2 Needs & Observations (Revised)**

These items represent the **first set of design-production needs** identified during the initial two weeks of implementation. Each need directly supports the core goals of this pipeline:  
**modularity, reusability, lifecycle clarity, and predictable development cost.**

---

## **1. Component Variant Architecture Needs**

### **1.1 Tab Component**
- Tüm **tab state’lerinin** (default, hover, active, disabled) belirlenmesi  
- **Multiple tab** gösterimi için “max-limit” davranışının tanımlanması  
- Taşma durumlarında (“more”, overflow) hangi UI davranışının uygulanacağının netleştirilmesi  
- Variant setinin üretimi (layout, spacing, indicator)

---

### **1.2 Input Field Component**
- Input alanlarının tüm **state’leri**: default, focus, filled, error, warning, disabled  
- Farklı input tipleri için variant’lar: text, numeric, masked input, multiline  
- Hata mesajı, helper text, icon inside gibi “compound” davranışların standardize edilmesi  
- Component variant setinin Figma’da production-friendly şekilde oluşturulması

---

### **1.3 Sidebar & Navigation**
- Sidebar menü öğelerinin tüm **variant’ları** (default, selected, expanded, collapsed)  
- Collapsible behavior: ikon + label düzeni  
- Submenu açılma/kapanma animasyon davranışının belirlenmesi  
- Rol bazlı görünürlük kuralları için tasarım ilkelerinin tanımlanması

---

### **1.4 İşlem Sonuç Statement Component (Success/Warning/Error)**
- İşlem sonrası gösterilen statement bileşeninin tüm durumlardaki  
  - renk  
  - ikon  
  - buton kombinasyonu  
- “Page-level” ve “inline-level” varyasyonlarının ayrıştırılması  
- Button + statement kombinasyonlarının reusable componeent haline getirilmesi

---

## **2. State / Status Standardization Needs**

### **2.1 State vs. Status Ayrımının Netleştirilmesi**
- **State = UI’nın anlık etkileşim durumu** (hover, active, disabled, focus)  
- **Status = İş nesnesinin iş durumunu temsil eden tanımlar** (Borç, Kalan, Kapalı, Açık, Beklemede)

Bu ayrım sistem genelinde şu hedefi sağlar:  
➡️ UI etkileşimi ile iş mantığı durumlarının karışmaması  
➡️ Renk, ikon, badge gibi öğelerin tutarlı ve öngörülebilir kullanımı

---

### **2.2 Status Renklerinin Standardizasyonu**
ERP’de sık geçen durumlar için sabit bir renk kodu belirlenmeli:

- **Borç**  
- **Kalan**  
- **Bakiye**  
- **Gecikmiş**  
- **Tamamlanmış**  
- **İptal / Reddedilmiş**  
- **Beklemede**

Hedef:  
➡️ Kullanıcı her modülde aynı statüyü aynı renk ile görsün.  
➡️ Geliştirici her statü için standardize edilmiş token’ı kullansın.

---

### **2.3 Icon Color Standardization**
- Primary icons  
- Secondary/neutral icons  
- Error/warning icons  
- Disabled icons  

Hedef:  
➡️ Modüller arasında ikon kullanımının tek standart üzerinden yürümesi  
➡️ Kontrast ve erişilebilirlik kurallarının korunması

---

## **3. Mode-Based & Card-Based Behaviors**

### **3.1 Mode Bazında UI Tanımları**
- View mode  
- Edit mode  
- Bulk-action mode  
- Required field behavior  

Her mod için:  
- renk  
- ikon  
- spacing  
- interaction davranışı  
net şekilde tanımlanmalı.

---

### **3.2 Card-Based Selection Patterns**
- Kart seçiminin default, hover, selected durumlarının standardizasyonu  
- İçerideki checkbox/icon davranışlarının tanımlanması  
- Table-row seçimi ile kart seçimi arasındaki tutarlılık

---

### 196. **ASSISTANT / NOTE:**

This is a **very real, very senior problem**.  
You’re basically asking: *“How do I extract value from a consultancy without letting them hijack, dilute, or mirror my internal system?”*  
That’s exactly how a **design lead / product owner** should think.

I’ll answer in **clear layers** so you can execute immediately.

---

## 1. First Principle: You Don’t Manage a Consultancy — You **Constrain** It

A consultancy should **never** be:
- A co-owner of your system
- A thought leader defining your standards
- A replacement for internal decision-making

They are:
> **Capacity + external validation under strict boundaries**

Your power comes from **what you don’t show**, not what you explain.

---

## 2. What You Share vs What You NEVER Share

### ❌ Do NOT Share (Internal IP)
These stay **inside Agito**, even if they ask:

- Your **internal framework structure** (A-EDF logic)
- Your **component lifecycle philosophy**
- Your **governance logic**
- Your **long-term design standardization roadmap**
- Your internal reasoning *why* things are built this way

If you share these, they will:
- Repackage them
- Echo them back
- Claim ownership
- Or unintentionally conflict later

---

### ✅ What You SHOULD Share (Output-Level Only)

You share **expectations**, not **mechanics**.

Think in terms of:
> **“What must be true when the work is delivered?”**

Not:
> “How we think / how we build internally”

---

## 3. How to Transfer Agito’s Expectations (Without Leaking Your System)

### Use This 3-Part Contract Model

### 1️⃣ **Design Constraints (Non-Negotiables)**  
You give them **hard constraints**, not philosophy.

Example:
- Uses Ant Design foundations
- Must support expert users (high data density, low friction)
- Must work for enterprise ERP scenarios
- Must be scalable across modules
- Must be production-ready (handoff quality matters)

These are **rules of the game**, not explanations.

---

### 2️⃣ **Acceptance Criteria (What “Good” Looks Like)**  
This is where you stay in control.

You define:
- What is considered complete
- What will be reviewed
- What will be rejected

Example:
- Screens must be structured with reusable logic (not one-off layouts)
- No purely visual decisions without rationale
- Flows must minimize repetitive input
- Error and empty states must be defined
- Design must be understandable without verbal explanation

You don’t say *how* to achieve this — only that **this is the bar**.

---

### 3️⃣ **Deliverables (Tangible Outputs Only)**

Ask for **artifacts**, not thinking.

Example deliverables:
- Screen sets for defined use cases
- Flow diagrams
- Component usage examples
- Interaction definitions
- Assumptions & open questions list

This ensures:
- You extract work
- You don’t absorb their ideology
- You keep synthesis internal

---

## 4. How You Manage Them Day-to-Day (Very Important)

### You Are the **Single Funnel**
- All feedback goes through you
- No direct access to engineering
- No side conversations
- No “we discussed with X” situations

This preserves:
- Authority
- Narrative control
- Strategic coherence

---

### Weekly Rhythm (Recommended)

**Weekly cadence:**
1. **Kickoff (15–30 min)**
   - Clarify scope
   - Re-state constraints
   - Define what will be reviewed next

2. **Mid-review (async or short)**
   - Spot misalignment early
   - Redirect without explaining too much

3. **Review (structured)**
   - You judge against expectations
   - Not against taste
   - Not against their past experience

---

## 5. How You Give Feedback Without Revealing Your Internal System

### ❌ Don’t say:
> “This doesn’t align with our framework”

### ✅ Say:
> “This introduces inconsistency across modules”  
> “This won’t scale when more workflows are added”  
> “This increases cognitive load for expert users”  
> “This will increase development cost”

These are **business & system arguments**, not design ideology.

---

## 6. How to Position Yourself (This Matters Politically)

You are **not**:
- “Managing design quality”

You are:
> **Representing Agito’s product system and production reality**

Use language like:
- “From Agito’s system perspective…”
- “Given our production constraints…”
- “At scale, this decision would create friction…”

This makes you:
- Untouchable
- Non-emotional
- Non-negotiable

---

## 7. What Success Looks Like (Your North Star)

A successful consultancy engagement means:
- They deliver usable assets
- You extract patterns and insights
- You integrate them into **A-EDF**
- They leave
- Your system remains coherent

If they walk away thinking:
> “Agito has a very clear product bar”

You won.

---

## 8. Final Strategic Warning (Read This Twice)

Consultancies **test leadership gaps**.

If:
- Standards are vague → they will define them
- Decisions are slow → they will push
- Authority is shared → they will expand scope

Your job is not to collaborate.
Your job is to **contain, extract, and integrate**.

---

- Create a **review scorecard** you’ll use against them
- Write the **kickoff script** you’ll say in the first meeting

Just tell me which one you want next.

# Consultancy Kickoff Script (First Meeting)

**Tone:** calm, confident, structured  
**Length:** ~8–10 minutes  
**Goal:** set boundaries, expectations, authority

---

## 1. Opening (Positioning – 1 minute)

> “Thanks for joining. Before we get into scope or execution details, I want to align on *how* we’ll work together and *what success looks like* for Agito.”

> “Agito builds enterprise ERP products with complex workflows, dense data, and expert users. This engagement is not about visual refresh or isolated screens — it’s about producing work that scales across modules and is production-ready.”

*(Pause. Let that sink in.)*

---

## 2. Your Role vs Their Role (Authority – 1 minute)

> “Internally, I’m responsible for ensuring design consistency, production feasibility, and system-level decisions across the product.”

> “Your role here is to support this system by delivering high-quality design outputs within defined constraints — not to redefine standards or introduce parallel approaches.”

> “All design decisions, feedback loops, and final approvals will go through me.”

This **closes the door** on side authority immediately.

---

## 3. Non-Negotiable Constraints (Rules of the Game – 2 minutes)

> “There are a few non-negotiables I want to be very clear about.”

> “First, this is an **enterprise, expert-user product**. Efficiency, clarity, and consistency matter more than expressiveness.”

> “Second, designs must be **scalable and reusable**. One-off layouts or screen-specific logic won’t be considered complete.”

> “Third, everything delivered must be **production-friendly** — structured, explainable, and usable by engineering without reinterpretation.”

> “Finally, we operate within Ant Design foundations, but how components are composed and reused is critical.”

No explanations. No philosophy. Just rules.

---

## 4. What “Good” Means at Agito (Acceptance Criteria – 2 minutes)

> “To be explicit, this is how we’ll evaluate the work.”

> “A design is successful if:
> - It can be reused across multiple modules
> - It minimizes repetitive input for expert users
> - States, errors, and edge cases are defined
> - The logic is clear without verbal explanation
> - It reduces downstream development and revision cost”

> “If a design looks good but fails on these points, we’ll iterate.”

This reframes taste into **system performance**.

---

## 5. Deliverables & Communication Model (Control – 1 minute)

> “We’ll work with clearly defined deliverables per phase — screens, flows, and documented assumptions.”

> “We’ll review work regularly, but feedback will be structured and centralized. There won’t be parallel discussions with engineering or stakeholders.”

> “Questions, uncertainties, and assumptions should be surfaced early — we prefer clarity over speed.”

---

## 6. How We’ll Collaborate (Psychological Safety Without Power Loss – 1 minute)

> “I value external perspective and challenge — but it needs to be grounded in enterprise context and scale.”

> “If something doesn’t align, I’ll explain *what* doesn’t work, not necessarily *how* we’ll solve it internally.”

> “The goal is to produce strong outcomes together, not to converge on the same methodology.”

This line protects your internal work without sounding defensive.

---

## 7. Close (Expectation Lock – 1 minute)

> “If we do this right, the outcome will be work that plugs cleanly into Agito’s system, accelerates development, and raises the quality bar across modules.”

> “If at any point expectations feel unclear, bring it to me directly. Alignment is more important than velocity.”

> “If this sounds good, we can move into scope and next steps.”

*(Stop talking.)*

Silence here is power.

---

## Final Advice (Very Important)

After the meeting:
- **Write a recap email** repeating:
  - Constraints
  - Acceptance criteria
  - Review process
- This becomes your **contractual memory**

If you want, next I can:
- Draft the recap email
- Create a **review scorecard** you’ll silently use
- Help you prepare **first review feedback language**

Go run the meeting.

# Agito — First Design Brief  
## PDF Policy / Document Editor for Insurers

### 1. Context (Why this exists)

Agito serves insurers who produce **high-volume, regulated, customer-facing documents** such as:

- Policies  
- Endorsements  
- Certificates  
- Annexes  

Today, these documents are:
- Hard to modify safely
- Prone to human error
- Difficult to standardize across products and insurers

The goal is **not** to build a “design tool”, but an **enterprise document production system**.

---

### 2. Problem Definition (What we are solving)

Insurers need a system that allows **authorized expert users** to:

- Edit PDF-based insurance documents
- While preserving:
  - Legal integrity
  - Structural consistency
  - Brand and layout rules
  - System-level constraints

The challenge is balancing:
- **Flexibility for experts**
- **Safety for regulated outputs**

---

### 3. Target Users (Non-negotiable)

This product is for:

- Policy operations specialists  
- Underwriting / product teams  
- Back-office insurance experts  

❗ Not end customers  
❗ Not casual users  
❗ Not designers  

These users:
- Work fast
- Know the domain
- Expect efficiency over discoverability
- Tolerate density if it saves time

---

### 4. Core Use Cases (Initial Scope)

You should assume workflows such as:

- Selecting a document template
- Editing structured sections (headers, clauses, tables, footers)
- Managing variable fields (policy number, dates, coverage values)
- Handling conditional content (if/else logic)
- Previewing final output
- Locking / approving documents
- Exporting final PDFs

Do **not** assume free-form canvas editing unless justified.

---

### 5. Key Constraints (Very Important)

Please design under these constraints:

1. **Enterprise-grade density**
   - Information-heavy layouts are expected
   - Minimal padding for aesthetics is not a goal

2. **Controlled editing**
   - Not every element is editable
   - Some content must be locked or rule-based

3. **Consistency over creativity**
   - Reuse patterns aggressively
   - Avoid unique interactions unless necessary

4. **Production reality**
   - Designs must scale across insurers and document types
   - One-off UI solutions are not acceptable

---

### 6. What “Good” Looks Like for Agito

We will evaluate outputs based on:

- Clarity of hierarchy in dense documents
- Speed of expert workflows
- Reusability of interaction patterns
- Clear handling of:
  - States
  - Errors
  - Permissions
- Feasibility for engineering handoff

If something looks good but doesn’t scale, it’s not done.

---

### 7. Deliverables (Phase 1)

We expect:

- High-level UX approach for PDF editing in enterprise context
- Key screen concepts (not exhaustive UI)
- Interaction logic for:
  - Editing vs preview
  - Locked vs editable areas
  - Error and validation states
- Clear assumptions and open questions

Visual polish is secondary to **structural clarity**.

---

### 8. Out of Scope (For Now)

- Branding exercises  
- Marketing-style visuals  
- End-user onboarding flows  
- Non-insurance use cases  

---

### 9. Collaboration Model

- Feedback and direction will come from Agito centrally
- Design decisions should be explained with rationale
- If assumptions are made, they must be explicit

---

### 10. Final Note (Tone Setter)

> “We are not trying to reinvent PDF editors.  
> We are designing a **safe, fast, and scalable document production tool for insurers**.”

---

## Why this brief works

- It **anchors them at system level**
- It prevents:
  - Figma-canvas fantasies
  - Dribbble-style thinking
  - End-user UX assumptions
- It positions **you** as product + system owner

---

- Or a **trap list** (common mistakes consultants make on document editors)
- Or a **first-review response script** when they inevitably over-design

Say the word.

## Why Apple Pages Came to Your Mind (and why that’s valid)

Apple Pages is strong at **one specific thing** that insurers desperately need:

- Strong hierarchy (sections, headers, body)
- Limited freedom, high safety
- Clear separation between:
  - Content
  - Structure
  - Style

That maps well to **insurance document reality**.

---

## How to Use Apple Pages as a Reference (Without Falling Into the Trap)

### ✅ What to Take from Apple Pages

#### 1. **Layout-first mindset**
Pages treats documents as:
- Sections
- Fixed zones
- Reusable structures

👉 For Agito:
- PDF = structured template
- Users edit **inside zones**, not on a free canvas

---

#### 2. **Inspector-based editing**
Pages avoids cluttering the canvas.

- Text settings → side inspector
- Table settings → contextual panel
- Section rules → centralized controls

👉 For Agito:
- Editing happens via:
  - Right-side panels
  - Context-aware controls
- Not floating toolbars everywhere

---

#### 3. **Guardrails, not freedom**
In Pages:
- You *can’t* easily break the document
- Layout collapse is hard
- Styles are enforced

👉 For insurers:
- This is gold.
- Legal + brand safety > creative freedom

---

#### 4. **Mode separation**
Pages is very clear about modes:
- Edit content
- Format content
- View / export

👉 For Agito:
- Editing mode vs Preview mode must be explicit
- No ambiguous “half-edit” states

---

### ❌ What NOT to Take from Apple Pages

This is critical — say this explicitly if needed.

- ❌ WYSIWYG free dragging
- ❌ Designer-oriented typography controls
- ❌ Consumer-level discoverability patterns
- ❌ “Make it pretty” defaults

Insurance ≠ document design.

You **do not** say:
> “We want something like Apple Pages”

You say:

> “Apple Pages is a reference for **how structured documents can be edited safely**, not for visual style or feature parity.”

- Control with you

- No feature-creep fantasies

# **Agito – PDF Basım & Editör Deneyimi**
## **Research Brief (Discovery & Benchmark Phase)**

**Project Type:** Enterprise PDF Editing & Printing Experience  
**Industry:** Insurance / ERP  
**Audience:** Consultancy Partner, Product, Engineering, UX  
**Owner:** Agito Product & Design  
**Prepared by:** Murat Çetin  

---

## 1. Background & Context

Agito develops **enterprise-grade insurance solutions** supporting complex workflows such as policy generation, endorsements, claims, renewals, and regulatory documentation.

A critical capability in these workflows is the **generation, editing, and printing of PDF documents** that are:
- Legally binding  
- Data-dense  
- Template-driven  
- Subject to strict formatting, branding, and regulatory rules  

Currently, the market expectation for insurers is **not a generic document editor**, but a **controlled, deterministic, and production-safe PDF editing experience**.

This research phase aims to establish **clear design, UX, and system expectations** for such a solution before any design or technical decisions are finalized.

---

## 2. Problem Definition

The problem space is **not simply “PDF editing”**, but:

- How insurers **safely edit and generate documents** without breaking structure, compliance, or data integrity.
- How **expert users** (operations, underwriting, claims, back-office) interact with documents under **time pressure and high accuracy requirements**.
- How document tools balance **flexibility vs. control** in enterprise environments.
- How production systems avoid **manual rework, layout breaks, and post-handoff corrections**.

There is currently **no shared internal reference** for:
- What “good” looks like in enterprise PDF editing  
- Which interaction models are acceptable  
- Which actions must be constrained or guided  

This research will establish that baseline.

---

## 3. Research Objectives

### Primary Objectives
1. **Map best-in-class approaches** to enterprise PDF editing and document generation.
2. Identify **interaction patterns** suitable for insurer workflows (editing, reviewing, approving, printing).
3. Understand how successful systems **limit user freedom intentionally** to prevent errors.
4. Define **UX expectations for expert users**, not casual consumers.

### Secondary Objectives
- Understand how document tools handle:
  - Templates
  - Data binding
  - Section locking
  - Versioning
  - Output reliability
- Identify common **anti-patterns** that increase error rates or operational cost.

---

## 4. Research Scope

### In Scope
- Enterprise PDF editors
- Document generation platforms
- Template-based editing systems
- Print-safe and compliance-oriented workflows
- Insurance-adjacent or ERP-level document tools

### Out of Scope
- Generic consumer text editors
- Free-form design tools (e.g., Figma, Canva)
- Word-processor-style document authoring (Microsoft Word-like behavior)
- Marketing or creative document tools

---

## 5. Target User Profile (Research Lens)

This research must **explicitly focus on expert users**, not general consumers.

**Expert User Characteristics:**
- High task repetition
- Strong domain knowledge
- Low tolerance for UI friction
- Zero tolerance for data or layout errors
- Outcome-driven, not exploration-driven

**Examples:**
- Underwriting operations
- Claims processing teams
- Policy issuance specialists
- Compliance & audit teams

Research insights must be evaluated through this lens.

---

## 6. Benchmark Categories & Evaluation Criteria

### A. Enterprise PDF Editing Tools
Examples: Adobe Acrobat, Foxit, Nitro  

**Evaluate for:**
- Editing boundaries (what users can vs. cannot change)
- Form & field handling
- Layout stability
- Print reliability
- Error prevention mechanisms

---

### B. Document Generation & Automation Platforms
Examples: Nintex, Templafy  

**Evaluate for:**
- Template governance
- Data-driven content insertion
- Conditional sections
- Role-based editing
- Version control

---

### C. Insurance / ERP-Adjacent Systems (if available)
Evaluate how domain-specific systems:
- Handle legal documents
- Prevent layout drift
- Guide users instead of trusting them

---

## 7. Key Research Questions

The consultancy is expected to answer:

1. **What interaction models work best** for editing insurer documents without breaking structure?
2. Where do leading tools **intentionally restrict user actions**, and why?
3. How do enterprise tools balance:
   - Flexibility
   - Speed
   - Compliance
4. What are the **common failure points** in PDF editing flows?
5. How do expert users:
   - Review
   - Edit
   - Approve
   - Print
   documents efficiently?

---

## 8. Expected Deliverables

### Mandatory Outputs
- **Benchmark matrix** (tools × capabilities)
- **Interaction pattern summaries**
- **Do / Don’t principles** for enterprise PDF editing
- **Annotated screenshots** highlighting critical UX decisions
- **Key insights & implications** for Agito

### Optional (Nice to Have)
- Conceptual flow diagrams
- Editing permission models
- Template vs. free-edit comparisons

---

## 9. Success Criteria

This research is successful if it:
- Creates **shared clarity** across Product, Design, and Engineering
- Reduces subjective discussions in later phases
- Enables **design decisions that are defensible** to CTO and stakeholders
- Supports Agito’s goal of building **production-safe, scalable ERP UX**

---

## 10. Positioning Note (Important)

This research is **not** intended to:
- Replicate existing tools
- Copy UI patterns blindly
- Design a creative editor

It is intended to:
> **Define the right level of control, structure, and interaction for insurer-grade document workflows.**

# **CTO Alignment Notes — PDF Printing & Editor Concept**
**Date:** 29.12.2025  
**Context:** Early alignment on PDF printing / editing capability for insurance use cases

---

## 1. What We Are *Not* Building

The CTO explicitly clarified several **non-goals**, which are critical to avoid wrong direction:

- ❌ Not an emailing tool (e.g. Mailchimp, Wix, campaign tools)
- ❌ Not a marketing or visual design tool
- ❌ Not a generic form builder as the primary goal
- ❌ Not a “free layout” design canvas

This is **not** about sending content.  
This **is** about **printing correctness, structure, and machine readability**.

---

## 2. Core Problem Space (Very Important)

Agito needs a **PDF printing & template editor** that supports **insurance-grade, machine-sensitive print workflows**.

### Key characteristics of these documents:
- Contain **barcodes** used by physical machines
- Some documents **must be printed as hardcopy**
- Barcodes are often placed at the **top of the page**
- **Policy number + page number** are encoded and tracked
- Machines:
  - Expect **fixed page counts**
  - Detect page boundaries (e.g. every 15 pages)
  - Separate documents automatically
- **Even a 1-pixel shift can break machine reading**
- Some outputs are still **dot-matrix prints**
- Government and agencies **scan and ingest** these documents

👉 **Layout drift = operational failure**

---

## 3. Existing Attempts & Constraints

- Tried with **OpenOffice**
- Issues observed:
  - Server cost
  - Stability under live load
  - Unexpected page breaks
  - Blank pages appearing due to data anomalies
- Dynamic data can:
  - Overflow
  - Push content to new pages
  - Insert unintended empty pages

👉 Printing systems **cannot tolerate anomalies**  
👉 We need **preventive mechanisms**, not manual fixes

---

## 4. What the CTO Is Asking For (Clear Direction)

> “I am looking for an editor to design print layouts.”

Not just PDFs — **print-safe PDF templates**.

### Desired capabilities:
- Almost **Word-like ease**, but with **much stricter control**
- Ability to:
  - Create templates
  - Improve visuals
  - Adjust layouts without going to agencies
- Non-designers should be able to:
  - Use **ready-made components**
  - Drag & drop safely
- Support:
  - Dynamic fields
  - Fixed areas
  - Non-shifting layouts
  - Barcode safety zones

This is a **controlled design environment**, not a free editor.

---

## 5. Important Clarification (Course Correction)

You and the CTO acknowledged that earlier thinking may have been misleading:

- Mixing:
  - Forms
  - Print
  - Fillable PDFs  
  may have **blurred the problem**

👉 The CTO explicitly said:

> “Don’t drift into forms.  
> Design a **printing editor concept**.”

This is a **print-first system**, not a form-first system.

---

## 6. Strategic Question to Answer (Make-or-Buy)

There are **two acceptable outcomes**:

1. DefineX finds a suitable solution  
2. Agito builds it from scratch  

What matters most:
> **We must have enough validated insight to make a confident decision.**

---

## 7. Immediate Action Items (Timeboxed)

- ⏱ Total time: **1.5 – 2 weeks**
- ⏱ First milestone: **Concept in 1 week**

### Your responsibilities:
- Research **printing principles**
- Understand:
  - Barcode constraints
  - Pagination logic
  - Dynamic data risks
  - Machine-readable print rules
- Talk to:
  - Handan
  - Onur (domain knowledge)

---

Not a solution yet — but **something concrete to react to**.

You need to:
- Ask the **right questions**
- Surface the **hidden constraints**
- Put **a concept in front of stakeholders**
  - To discuss

# **Problem Framing Canvas**
**Project:** Insurance-grade PDF Printing & Editor  
**Owner:** Agito  
**Date:** 29.12.2025

---

## 1. Problem Statement (Core Framing)

> Agito lacks a **print-safe, insurance-grade PDF editor** that allows non-designers to create and manage visually improved but **structurally deterministic** documents.  
>  
> Existing tools fail to guarantee layout stability, barcode accuracy, pagination correctness, and machine readability under dynamic data conditions — creating operational risk, rework, and cost.

---

## 2. Why This Problem Exists (Root Causes)

### Design & Tooling
- General-purpose tools (OpenOffice, Word-like editors) allow **uncontrolled layout behavior**
- Layouts shift due to:
  - Dynamic content
  - Overflow
  - Auto-pagination
- 1-pixel deviations can break downstream machine processing

### Domain-Specific Constraints
- Insurance documents must be:
  - Machine-readable
  - Barcode-sensitive
  - Page-count aware
- Printing machines:
  - Expect fixed structure
  - Detect page boundaries
  - Fail silently on anomalies

### Organizational Reality
- Designers and agencies are costly
- Non-designers need to safely produce documents
- Current workflows are:
  - Manual
  - Fragile
  - Hard to validate upfront

---

## 3. Who Is Affected (Primary Stakeholders)

### Internal
- Operations teams (printing, distribution)
- Product & engineering teams
- Business users creating documents
- QA & compliance stakeholders

### External
- Insurance agencies
- Government institutions
- Printing vendors
- End customers (indirectly)

---

## 4. User Archetypes (Simplified)

### 🧑‍💼 Business Operator (Non-Designer)
- Wants to:
  - Update layouts
  - Improve visuals
  - Create templates
- Needs:
  - Safety
  - Predictability
  - Ready-made components

### 🏭 Machine / System (Implicit User)
- Requires:
  - Absolute layout stability
  - Fixed barcode positions
  - Deterministic pagination
- Has **zero tolerance** for ambiguity

---

## 5. What We Are NOT Solving (Explicit Non-Goals)

- ❌ Emailing / campaign tools (Wix, Mailchimp)
- ❌ Marketing design tools
- ❌ Free-form layout editors
- ❌ Generic form builders as the main solution
- ❌ Visual creativity over operational safety

This is **not a design playground**.  
This is a **controlled production system**.

---

## 6. Key Constraints (Non-Negotiables)

- Layout must **never drift**
- Barcode zones must be:
  - Fixed
  - Protected
- Pagination rules must be:
  - Deterministic
  - Predictable
- Dynamic data must:
  - Be constrained
  - Fail safely
- Tool must support:
  - Server-side generation
  - Scale
  - Stability

---

## 7. What Success Looks Like (Outcome Definition)

### Functional Success
- Non-designers can create print-safe PDFs
- Templates behave consistently under dynamic data
- No unexpected page shifts or blank pages

### Operational Success
- Reduced rework
- Fewer production errors
- Faster iteration without risk

### Strategic Success
- Clear decision: **build vs buy**
- Validated concept that stakeholders can react to
- A scalable foundation for future document workflows

### 218. **ASSISTANT / NOTE:**

**Short answer:**  
**Jotform is *not* a core benchmark for the PDF printing/editor problem Agito is solving — but it *is* a useful benchmark for a related piece (form data capture).**  
It shouldn’t be a primary benchmark for the print editor itself.

Here’s why — explained clearly and succinctly:

---

# ✅ **Why Jotform *isn’t* a Core Benchmark (for your print editor)**

### 1) Jotform is a **form builder**, not a **print layout editor**
Jotform shines at:
- Creating forms (web forms, surveys)
- Capturing structured data
- Generating basic PDFs from form submissions

But it does *not* focus on:
- Layout *precision*
- Print *determinism*
- Barcode & machine reading
- Fixed pagination
- Page security zones
- Template governance for high-stakes legal documents

These are **core requirements** for Agito’s printing editor.

> **Conclusion:**  
Jotform is a form solution; not a print layout engine.

---

# ✅ **Where Jotform *is* a Useful Reference**

Your earlier problem scoping included:
- Form → Print
- Fillable PDF considerations

In that context:

### Jotform is relevant for:
✔ Form → PDF data binding  
✔ Generating a **fillable PDF** from structured input  
✔ Understanding user experience for non-technical users creating **data templates**

So **Jotform informs the “data entry → document generation” interaction**, not the **print editor** itself.

**This matters for:**
- Understanding how users want to bind data to document templates
- UX patterns of non-designer users
- Form-based data flows

---

# 🧠 **How to Use Jotform in Your Research Brief**

If you need to include it, frame it like this:

> **Benchmark Category:** Data Capture → Template Population  
> *Representative example:* Jotform (form-driven PDF generation UX)  
> *What it teaches us:* Data binding, user flow simplicity, field validation, and lightweight PDF generation workflows — NOT layout precision or printing determinism.

---

# 📌 **Better Benchmarks for Your Core Problem**

For the print editor itself, use tools/platforms that demonstrate **structured print-safe document creation, deterministic layout, and machine-aware outputs**:

### 🧾 Core Print & Layout Benchmarks
- **Adobe Acrobat Pro** – strong printing and PDF editing with structure  
- **Foxit PDF Editor** – enterprise editing  
- **Nitro PDF** – enterprise editing + workflow  
- **OnlyOffice** – structured editing with online UX

## CTO Decision Memo (One Paragraph)

After evaluating existing tools across form builders (Jotform), visual editors (PUCK), and print-focused software (Adobe Acrobat), it is clear that none address Agito’s core need: **insurance-grade, deterministic PDF production that can be visually edited by non-designers without breaking print constraints**. Form builders optimize for data collection, not output correctness; visual editors optimize for layout freedom, not pagination, barcodes, or machine-readability; and traditional PDF tools require expert users and lack guardrails. This is not a tooling gap but a **category gap**. Therefore, the recommended direction is to define and validate a **Print-First Document Editor concept** purpose-built for insurance workflows—prioritizing output reliability, constrained layout, and dynamic data safety over design freedom—before deciding whether to build in-house or partner with a consultancy.

---

## What We Will **NOT** Build (Explicit Non-Goals)

To avoid scope creep and architectural mistakes, the following are **out of scope by design**:

1. **Not a Form Builder**  
   We will not build a Jotform-like data collection tool. User input, submissions, and workflows are secondary. The primary artifact is a **print-safe document**, not a form.

2. **Not a Website / Page Builder**  
   We will not build a PUCK- or Webflow-style free layout editor. Absolute positioning freedom, arbitrary blocks, and responsive web logic are incompatible with print determinism.

3. **Not a General-Purpose Word or InDesign Replacement**  
   We will not replicate Word, Pages, or InDesign. These tools assume expert users and allow layout states that silently break barcodes, pagination, and scanning machines.

4. **Not a “Design Tool” for Designers**  
   The system is not optimized for creative design. It is optimized for **safe composition by non-designers**, with strong constraints and predefined components.

5. **Not a Fillable PDF Platform**  
   Interactive PDFs, user-editable fields, and post-delivery manipulation are out of scope. Output must be **final, locked, and predictable**.

---

## Implied Product North Star (for alignment)

> **A constrained, print-first PDF editor that allows insurance teams to visually assemble compliant, machine-readable documents without risking pagination, barcodes, or scanning integrity.**

## Why “Form Builder” is a Dangerous Add-On (Structurally)

A **form builder** and a **print-safe document editor** solve **different core problems**:

| Dimension | Form Builder | Insurance Print Editor |
|-------|-------------|----------------|
| Primary goal | Collect data | Produce legally & machine-readable output |
| Layout model | Responsive / flow-based | Fixed page / deterministic |
| Failure tolerance | High | Near zero |
| User mindset | External end-user | Internal expert operator |
| Output | JSON / submissions | PDF for machines & legal archiving |
| Risk profile | UX errors | Legal, financial, regulatory errors |

Trying to merge them creates **architectural contradiction**.

---

## The Hidden Risk You Must Call Out

If you allow “form builder” now, these WILL happen:

1. **Responsive expectations leak in**  
   → “Why can’t this reflow on mobile?”

2. **Free layout requests appear**  
   → “Let users move fields anywhere”

3. **Validation logic starts dominating UI**  
   → You stop designing documents, start building rules engines

4. **Ownership confusion**
   - Is this for agents?
   - Customers?
   - Operations?
   - Compliance?

5. **Benchmark confusion**
   - Jotform
   - Typeform
   - Acrobat Forms  
   None of which solve print determinism.

This is how products lose identity.

# Master Context Document  
**Project:** Agito Enterprise Fillable Document Platform  
**Audience:** Product, Design, Engineering, External Consultants  
**Authoritative Context:** Final  
**Purpose:** Establish shared understanding of *why* this product exists, *what* it is (and is not), and *how* it will be built.

---

## 1. Executive Context — Why This Project Exists

Agito operates in the **insurance ERP domain**, where core business processes depend on **highly structured, machine-readable, legally sensitive documents**.

These documents are:
- Generated dynamically from ERP systems
- Printed on **dot-matrix / industrial printers**
- Scanned, split, and processed by **machines**
- Filled by **external users** (customers, agents, institutions)
- Subject to **strict layout, pagination, and barcode rules**

### The problem:
There is **no reliable internal tool** that allows Agito (or its insurance clients) to:
- Design **print-safe, machine-compatible PDF documents**
- Embed **dynamic ERP data**
- Control **exact layout, pagination, and barcode behavior**
- Enable **external users to fill documents safely**
- Do all of the above **without agencies, Word hacks, or broken tools**

Existing solutions (Word, OpenOffice, form builders, website builders) **fail** because they:
- Reflow layouts unpredictably
- Break machine readability
- Are not ERP-aware
- Treat documents as “content” or “forms,” not operational artifacts

This creates:
- High operational risk
- Manual fixes
- Broken prints
- Scanner failures
- Costly rework

---

## 2. Core Problem Definition (Framed Precisely)

> **Insurance companies need a way to design, generate, distribute, and collect fillable PDF documents that behave like machines expect — not like websites or forms.**

This is **not** a form problem.  
This is **not** a CMS problem.  
This is **not** a website builder problem.

This is a **document engineering problem**.

---

## 3. Product Definition — What We Are Building

### Product Type
**An internal document composition platform** that produces:
- Fixed-layout
- Print-safe
- Machine-readable
- ERP-connected
- Fillable PDF documents

### Mental Model
Think:
- **Adobe InDesign precision**
- **ERP data binding**
- **Controlled fillable fields**
- **Operational governance**

Not:
- Jotform
- Website builders
- Freeform editors

---

## 4. Non-Negotiable Product Principles (Guardrails)

These principles override feature discussions.

1. **The document is the product**
2. **Layout never reflows**
3. **Machines are first-class users**
4. **External users only fill — never design**
5. **PDF is the final authority**
6. **Every output must be printable**
7. **Finalized sprint designs serve as documentation**

If a feature violates one of these → it is out of scope.

---
